The contract requires exactly-rounded output on the full finite FP16 domain, so the decisive test is an exhaustive bit-exact sweep of all 65536 finite FP16 inputs. I'll record that claim and probe it.

message.reasoning_content: Kernel looks correct for exact rounding: computes in FP32 using stable form, div_rn, cvt.rn.f16.f32. Potential failure: FP32 intermediate may not be precise enough to decide ties — e.g., value exactly halfway between FP16 values; FP32 error could flip rounding. The reference computes FP64 sigmoid then rounds once. So need probe: sweep all 65536 finite FP16 inputs? N max 131072 — could split into two tensors of all finite FP16 values and compare bits with reference. Also check contiguity, negative x: for x<0, sigmoid = exp/(1+exp) — computed as numerator=exponential where exponential = exp(-|x|). Correct. x=+0: exp(0)=1, numerator=1, value=0.5 ✓. Subnormal output: cvt.rn.f16.f32 handles rounding to subnormals with RNE. div_rn is correctly rounded FP32 division. The only concern: exp in FP32 vs true exp error up to ~1ulp FP32; combined with division error up to 0.5ulp FP32, could total error exceed half an FP16 ulp boundary near ties. Probe exhaustively.
